Well, since I answered this question with inventory management, I suppose I'll answer here as well.

One problem with a tiny inventory is that it punishes you early in the game. You have no idea what you're doing, you're just collecting cool stuff. Then your inventory is full and you're forced to sell things, dump things, or otherwise destroy them before you even know what's really worth keeping or using.

I think this ancient Diablo type system where everything just gets dumped into a "sack" and then you have to sort through it sucks. Better games split things up by various categories, but why not have sub-categories? I'm fine with all of the stuff that goes on my character going into a bucket but then it should be split up by type - head armor, foot, hand, chest, weapons, etc. If the game supports sets, let me organize things that way too. Don't make me have to re-confirm the status of every stupid set I'm collecting every time I happen upon something. It'd actually be nice to get a little notification when you get an item that's part of a set - you have x/y items for this set, you need - helmet, gloves to complete the set.

Inventory should be limitless, I think it frequently isn't because the inventory management tools are always so sparse. Make them more robust. Make it easy to sort things, automate comparisons between what I have now and what's in my inventory, color code the results. Stop with the "rarity" coloring. Who cares how rare it is? It's all random, sometimes really rare things suck, sometimes "common" things end up being pretty cool. Why even show me the absolute values for things? What's the point? Just show me a value relative to what's in my inventory. +/- some number. I can still compare between different items with that number - this is +5 and that's +10, obviously the latter one is better.
